items.title: Jamey Aebersold interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, September 26, 2022
items.q: Dave Brubeck comped on my Dave Brubeck play-a-long. And afterwards he said, “Jamey, that’s the hardest thing I’ve ever had to do.”

ctx.x: Terrific story. And I wanted to speak about “So What” actually but a little later. Now we’ve got two laters. So this developed into this idea of recording a piano trio and assembling what you felt was enough information to get people started. Did you have trouble in a couple of things. First of all do you recall if the piano trio had to do some adjusting because they weren’t backing anybody up? They were just playing. Was that difficult for them at first?

In the early stages I don’t think it was because we all, none of us really knew what we were doing. We were trying to lay down some tracks and I probably told the piano player don’t play too busy. And drummer, don’t take a solo, delineate the form, eight bar © Fillius Jazz Archive -9-

phrases, four bar phrases, whatever. And bass player, just walk. You know? And I don’t even think we did any bossa novas on the very, very first one. I doubt it. They were probably all kind of swing. But later, once we moved in and you had people like Hal Galper who you’ve interviewed, and some other ones, they found — Ronnie Mathews on the piano up in New York.
